blockers.quote: At home, Aarav's waiting. A fee slip for a cricket academy. And one question. For you. The one who can see the numbers.
blockers.why: story #11: the first two sentences caption the shot on line 98 (Aarav at your door with the slip). This is the same fault the owner fixed on the bus line on 2026-11-10: a line over a shot should say what the shot can't.
blockers.fix: Line 99: "One question. For the one who can see the numbers." Then carry the academy on line 105: "Zero point two. Against a cricket academy's fees. The family's money. And the biggest number is the right choice. Isn't it?"

blockers.why: story #11: the hold on line 152 has just played the ball off a bat, and the narrator names the sound again. Your own narration notes already allow the effect alone. It also steps on the owner's 2026-11-10 note that the last line is "Every night. And you know the number."
blockers.fix: Cut the spoken line and let the line-152 effect carry it. If the lane must be placed, change the line-152 sound to a crisp thwack and a far-off kid's laugh, with no narration before line 155.

suggestions.quote: Here's how it works. Each chip is one person's chance at the one thing they'd choose... with nobody watching. It never tells you what that thing is.
suggestions.fix: This is where I would leave, at about 0:35. "Here's how it works" sounds like a teacher, and lines 30 and 31 give three rule facts in a row while you sit still. Cut "Here's how it works." and start on the chip: "Each chip: one person's chance at the one thing they'd choose... with nobody watching." Then keep line 31 as it is.

suggestions.quote: Your own number moves. You've seen it. His... you just read.
suggestions.fix: I had to rewind this one; on a single listen, "you just read" does not land. Try: "Yours moved when you moved. His... you read like a verdict." It ties back to line 86's "verdict".

Line 134 already shows you pull out the bat and knock, and the line-136 hold shows Aarav taking it, so the narrator is captioning the answer to the choice. Cut it and go straight from line 133 to the 4 s hold.

keep.quote: You can't borrow someone's odds. Only their apron.
But a verdict doesn't move. Yours did.
The last bus home. And you can't stop reading them. Like timetables.
